newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers group says Fed action wrong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers group says Fed action wrong.

text.p: The National Association of Manufacturers said the Federal Reserve's action to raise interest rates was wrong and would impede economic growth.
"It is a regrettable and serious mistake," NAM said in a statement.
"The Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates was simply wrong. It will impede economic growth and make life tougher on consumers and job-creating businesses," the trade group said.

NAM said there were three reasons why interest rates should not have been raised: There was no sign of any acceleration in inflation, there was no evidence that labor markets were too tight and finally there was little danger the economy would overheat in the short term.
The economy's potential output was closer to 2.8 percent due to higher productivity, NAM said, rather than the 2.3 percent frequently estimated.

It said the economy in the first half of 1997 appeared to be slowing down and settling in equilibrium. "Under these circumstances there was no reason to raise rates," NAM Vice President Paul Huard said.
